shalin supported my husband and i throughout the pregnancy and birth of our first child as our doula, evidence based birth childbirth educator, and lactation educator. 

hiring shalin was one of the best decisions we made in preparation for welcoming our baby. as our doula, her impartial and unwavering support guided us through decision making during our pregnancy and helped us to advocate for the prenatal care and birth preferences we desired. shalin's evidence based birth course equipped us with the knowledge and tools needed for a variety of birth experiences. this left my husband and i feeling more prepared in our roles both as the birthing person and support person leading up to the birth of our baby. lastly, shalin's one-on-one prenatal lactation course helped me to feel much more confident about breastfeeding for the first time knowing that i could trouble shoot common challenges and that i was equipped with the knowledge and resources needed for differing eventualities.

about a month before our estimated due date the covid 19 pandemic hit, causing our hospital to restrict visitors and not allow doulas in the birthing space. shalin calmly and proactively navigated this stressful situation, creating a library of online resource videos and offering virtual support for families in labor once they reached the hospital. she helped us to reformulate our plan for labor and birth to adapt to this less than ideal situation - helping us to regain a sense of control and support and reduce anxiety. 

on our baby's birthday shalin supported us in-person as we labored at home and then seamlessly transitioned to supporting us virtually via zoom and text once we moved to the hospital. her support throughout our pregnancy and birth played a huge role in helping us to achieve the positive and empowering birth experience we had envisioned.

i did not want to cause a ruckus while there were people waiting for their surgery. when i was alone with the coughing women i went over to her and asked if she would please wash her hands after she blew her nose, and dispose of the tissue in the trash 2 ft away, and to keep the mask over her nose. she just said no and closed her eyes. 
i went over to the receptionist and told her, she said she could not ask the lady to do that. so, i said , can you ask the lady to wait outside or in her car. she said no. i gave her my phone number and said i would be in my car to call me, which she did.

the most unprofessional doctor's office i have had the misfortune to come across.

it took a long time to get a referral from my pcp and insurance to see an endocrinologist. they ultimately referred me to dr. jelen. after seeing the reviews here, i was worried, but made my appointment anyways, hoping for the best.

the doctor's office sent out multiple text messages and phone messages, all of which i answered in order to confirm my appointment. the morning of my appointment, i called to ask if the doctor was running on time (due to reviews here on yelp that reported her running two to three hours late). the receptionist said sorry, but my appointment had to be canceled because of "covid19." i asked why this wasn't the case the day before (when i confirmed my appointment), but she just reiterated that it was unforeseen until that very morning. that didn't make sense, but whatever.

she rescheduled me to a telemedicine appointment the following week, which i said was fine, even though i was already 9 month pregnant and the appointment was on my due date. a week later, i call thirty minutes before my appointment to make sure it was a telemedicine appointment, and not in the office, in order to make sure everyone was on the same page. she confirmed the telemedicine format to be the case, and confirmed the time of my appointment (11:45am). i wait. and wait. and wait ... i call again, to make sure they have my number right. yes, they have my number, but the doctor is running late. the receptionist said i was the first patient she would call when back in the office.

ok, so i wait longer, glued to my phone so i don't miss the call. after 2pm (2.5 hours after my appointment was supposed to start), i call again. they say they were canceling my appointment and i would have to reschedule, because of technical issues with telemedicine. i say i don't want to reschedule since my baby is due any day now, please can i talk to the doctor on the phone, like the receptionist and i were doing? she said no, and then seemed to perk up when i reminded her i was pregnant, and told me that the doctor doesn't see pregnant patients! dr. jelen's office and the referring office both knew i was pregnant, i mentioned it repeatedly. anyways, it barely matters because as i'm due any day now, i obviously won't be pregnant for long. i pleaded to speak with the doctor, or at least a manager. after a significant time on hold, i was transferred to "james" who refused to give me his last name and claimed to be the office manager. he talked over me, told me my opinion of their office didn't matter because i wasn't an "established patient," said in an accusatory way that all the bad reviews online were from people "like me" (whatever that meant, i just want health care, which i pay for). i couldn't get a word in; i tried repeatedly to please speak with the doctor, but he told me to get a different doctor and hung up on me!

now i don't know what to do except to complain to my insurance. i have been hypothyroid over a year, and have been trying this whole time to be worked up, but still haven't been seen. even if i get referred to another doctor's office, i'll have to wait months again to get an appointment. i'm an md (not an endocrinologist) and can't imagine treating patients this way. as a patient, you're powerless to get seen by this doctor. unbelievably unprofessional.

tl; dr: at the time of this writing, over 88% of her yelp reviews are 1-star. there is a serious problem here. run!

unfortunately, this facility is one of the very few imaging centers that offer "open" mris for patients who are unable to undergo/tolerate traditional "closed" mri machines (which are readily available and typically preferred).  

my office recently encountered a somewhat absurd and infuriating response from the staff of elk grove open mri in regards to our attempts to schedule a patient for his mri without contrast a few months back.

the medical staff at this facility was not only unprofessional, but demanded that our patient go through both the mri with iv contrast as well as without, simply due to their facility having already received an authorization from the patient's insurance for both types of mris. 

even after ordering provider explained and explicitly requested for imaging facility to perform testing without contrast, as iv contrast mri was deemed unnecessary and inappropriate with patient not having surgical hardware present in spine. not to mention causing undue pain to the patient as the procedure of performing mri with iv contrast requires puncturing the skin/arm of the patient with a needle in order to access a vein for contrast administration)

it's very unfortunate that a medically licensed provider has to plead with an imaging facility to not perform medically unnecessary testing, nor put a patient through further invasive type medical procedures that are unwarranted. much less charge an insurance company for testing that is no longer appropriate.

i've actually added a extra star, only due to the fact that our office has had not further issues with this facility since this unfortunate encounter. however, we have since advised and referred our patient's to dri instead (who are exceptional by the way)

sincerely, 
a concerned medically licensed provider

doc_text: back in february i injured my knee during training. i powered through the pain and continued training for about a week. it was at the point where the swelling was so bad that walking was unbearable. i finally went to seek medical attention and was told that i need to ice, rest and elevate my knee. i was also prescribed ointment for the arthritis which managed the pain a bit but the swelling continued. i had a couple sports massages done but my knee would swell up again. some of my friends told me to try acupuncture. i contacted a few places and dr patel was the first one to respond. after two weeks of pain, i met with dr patel. i explained the circumstances to my injury and right off the bat she explained what the underlying issue is and off i went for my first acupuncture treatment. she also did the cupping treatment and wow, i felt the difference immediately. not only did the swelling decrease but i was able to put more weight on that leg and walk without limping. i went the following week for another treatment and dr patel said i have sciatica which may be the root of the swelling and pain down my leg. covid-19 came into play and my sessions were on hold for a few weeks. my sciatica was in full effect and getting a good nights sleep was challenging. when dr patel's office opened up again i began seeing her once a week and could feel a difference after each session. the sharp pain i was feeling on the inside of my knee had subsided significantly and only slight swelling would occur after long walks or workouts. i wish i had started acupuncture and cupping treatments sooner.  and  i can't say enough about the personal care and professionalism i received from dr patel each time i go in. she's always determined to make sure i'm pain free and i am certainly on my way. thank you dr patel for healing me and allowing me to continue my training when i was close to throwing in the towel.
